713015.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰunkʰanō, from the nasal-infixed present *dʰu-n-gʰ- of Proto-Indo-European *dʰewgʰ- (“to hit, produce, yield”), whence also τεύχω (teúkhō, “produce”).

713071.t: From Proto-Hellenic *údōr, from Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥ (genitive *wednós (“of water”)), with ω (ō) from the plural), from the root *wed- (whence also ὕω (hū́ō, “to water, to let rain, to rain”)).

713075.t: From earlier υἱύς (huiús); see there for more.

713059.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂yu-gʷih₃- (“long life”) or Proto-Indo-European *h₁su-gʷih₃- (“good life”) with -ής (-ḗs, “adjective suffix”); the former derivation is favored by Beekes and Weiss.

713053.t: From ὑβρίζω (hubrízō, “to act violently”) + -τικός (-tikós), from ὕβρις (húbris, “violence”).

713012.t: From τρώγω (trṓgō, “to bite; to eat”), through the concept of an animal chewing a hole.

713077.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *swel-, *sel- (“firewood, wood, beam”), and compared with Latin silva (“forest”), English sill, Latvian sile (“trough”).

713045.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *sew-? Proto-Indo-European *sewH-? Proto-Indo-European *suH- Proto-Hellenic *hūs Ancient Greek ὗς (hûs) Proto-Indo-European *-nós Ancient Greek -νος (-nos) Proto-Indo-European *-is Proto-Indo-European *-h₂…

713022.t: From Proto-Hellenic *túpt͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewp- (“to push, beat”). Cognates include Sanskrit तोपति (tópati, “to hurt”), Latin stupeō and Old Church Slavonic тъпати (tŭpati).

713034.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰúkʰā, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewgʰ- (“to produce, yield”). Equivalent to τυγχάνω (tunkhánō, “to happen”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

713026.t: Perhaps a borrowing of a Lydian word for “king” or a similar word in another language of Asia Minor.

713081.t: From Proto-Indo-European *usmé, with regular rough breathing ῾ (h) before initial υ (u).

713076.t: From ὑλάω (huláō, “to bark”) + a suffix -ακτέω (-aktéō) also seen in ἀγανακτέω (aganaktéō, “to feel vexed”), likely from an onomatopoeic root *ul- also reflected in Latin ululō (“to howl”), ulula (“screech owl”), Sanskrit उलूक (úlūka, “owl”), and…

713029.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tūrós (whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀶𐀫 (tu-ro /⁠tūrós⁠/)), probably from Proto-Indo-European *tuh₂-ró-s, from *tewh₂- (“to swell”).

713051.t: Unknown; possibly Pre-Greek, given its unusual shape and the lack of a convincing Indo-European etymology.

713031.t: Adjectival formation in -λός (-lós) from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewbʰ- (“deep, hazy, foggy”). Cognates include Old Irish dub (“dark”), Old English deaf (English deaf), Albanian dudum.

713063.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ugrós, from Proto-Indo-European *wegʷ- (“wet, moist”). Cognate with Latin ūvidus.

713002.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *trewH-p-, a p-extension of a putative *trewH- (“to rub”), and cognate with τρύω (trúō, “to wear down”) and Proto-Slavic *tryti (“to rub”).

713083.t: From the root of ὑμεῖς (hūmeîs, “you”, plural) + -τερος (-teros, contrastive adjective suffix).

713048.t: Of Pre-Greek or other Mediterranean substrate origin and possibly related to Latin vaccinium. Note the Pre-Greek suffix -ινθ- (-inth-).

713019.t: Traditionally regarded as a formation from τύπτω (tŭ́ptō, “to strike, beat, smite”) + -ανον (-ănon), similar to that of ὄργανον (órganon, “instrument, sense organ”).

713049.t: According to Furnée, a Pre-Greek word, due to the variation "α/ε".

713033.t: Derived from the verb τύφω (túphō, “to smoke”).

713095.t: From the verb ὑπακούω (hupakoúō, “give ear, hearken”).

713011.t: Enlargement of τρύω (trúō), in the same manner as terms such as σμήχω (smḗkhō).

713094.t: From ὑπο- (hŭpo-, “sub-, hypo-”) + αἶθρος (aîthros, “clear chill air”).

713008.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰrupʰā́, from the root of θρύπτω (thrúptō, “to shatter; to be wanton”) (from *tʰrúpʰyō.
